Ethanol concentration is 4–5% after saccharification and fermentation. In the final step, distillation and molecular sieve adsorption are used to recover ethanol from the raw fermentation beer and produce 99.5% ethanol. The beer column bottoms stream, containing water, lignin, and other organics, is sent to a series of triple effect evaporators. The resulting slurry is filtered and wet lignin from the filters may be combusted for generated electricity as a co- product. B.13 RENEWABLE H | RWGS | E-METHANOL 2 In this process, methanol is produced from renewable H and CO captured from point sources 2 2 through a two-step pathway. In the first step, H and CO with 1:1 molar ratio is fed to a reverse 2 2 water gas shift (RWGS) reactor, where CO is partially converted to CO. The unconverted CO is 2 2 separated into an acid gas removal unit using Selexol technology and recycled back to the RWGS reactor. The syngas from RWGS, with a H :CO ratio about 2:1, is then sent to the methanol 2 synthesis and purification unit to produce high purity methanol similar to that in the methanol: biomass gasification pathway. B.14 RENEWABLE H | HB | GREEN AMMONIA 2 In this process, ammonia is produced from renewable hydrogen via water electrolysis and nitrogen from air separation via cryogenic distillation. To obtain high-purity nitrogen, dry air is compressed to 6–7 MPa and precooled via heat transfer between the warm feeding air and the outgoing cold air. Then precooled air goes through an expansive valve into a cryogenic heat exchanger where the air is cooled to -184°C. Then a distillation column is employed to separate the air components based on the boiling points. As a result, the pure oxygen from the distillation column will be treated as a co-product. B-4 The mature Haber–Bosch (HB) process is considered here to produce ammonia via the obtained pure hydrogen and nitrogen. The mixture of hydrogen and nitrogen with 3:1 molar ratio is first compressed to 30°C and 275 bar, then combined with the unreacted recycle stream to further compress and heat exchange with the reaction effluent to reach the reactor condition at about 290 bar, 450°C. The reaction is limited by the thermodynamic equilibrium and the typical conversion yield range is 25–35 mol%. To further separate the product and unreacted hydrogen and nitrogen, the reactor effluent is first cooled to 40°C via heat exchangers and then separated with a flash tank. The liquid ammonia is at the flash bottom with a purity of 97mol%, while the gas stream including the unreacted feedstocks will be recycled back to the system for increase the conversion rate.
